title: Unvalidated HTTP request body field passed as C string across cgo boundary
detail: `ApplyProfile()` decodes the HTTP request body into `req.Label` (line 25) and converts it directly to a C string with `C.CString(req.Label)` at line 30, passing it to `C.aurora_profile_label()` at line 32 without any length check, null-byte rejection, or content validation. The C function is defined in the cross-component header `aurora-network/src/profile_label.h`, which is not present in this repository. If that function copies the string into a fixed-size buffer without bounds checking, an HTTP caller can trigger a buffer overflow or memory corruption by sending an arbitrarily long `label` value. The `/v1/profile/apply` route is token-gated (see routes.go), but insider or stolen-token scenarios still expose this path.
